newsitem.title: USA: Las Vegas salesman sentenced for insider trading.
newsitem.headline: Las Vegas salesman sentenced for insider trading.

text.p: A Las Vegas insurance salesman was sentenced Friday to one year in prison for his part in an insider trading scheme using information from the Wall Street law firm Cravath, Swaine, & Moore.

Manhattan U.S. District Court Judge John Martin sentenced Edward Eizman, who pleaded guilty in April to one count of conspiracy to commit securities fraud, to 12 months and one day in a minimum-security prison.
The judge said Eizman committed his crimes "for no reason other than greed." But he ordered the sentence delayed for 60 days to let Eizman attend a sports tournament for a youth group he works for.

Eizman admitted using information on potential mergers he received from a friend at the law firm and tipping off 11 friends and relatives. Prosecutors alleged he earned $132,016 in illegal profits and that his associates made $165,127 in the scheme, which generated nearly $1 million in illegal profits.
Last year Eizman's friend, Richard Woodward, a former senior associate at Cravath, Swaine, & Moore, and his brother, John, pleaded guilty to criminal insider trading charges.

Federal investigators said Woodward worked on mergers and acquisitions and passed on tips regarding CBS Inc., ITT Corp., Johnson & Johnson, King World Productions Inc., Ciba-Geigy, Bristol-Myers Squibb and S. G. Warburg.
